common_name: Tranquillity Rose (David Austin English Shrub Rose)

planting.note: Set out own-root or container plants in spring or fall in full sun with good air circulation; Tranquillity is an almost thornless David Austin rose prized for clean, healthy, disease-resistant foliage.

directions: Plant in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil enriched with compost, and prune canes back by about a third in late winter to encourage strong new flowering wood. Introduced by David Austin in 2012, Tranquillity opens creamy buds lightly tinged with yellow into large, perfectly formed white rosette blooms packed with over a hundred neatly arranged petals, carrying a light, fresh, fruity fragrance. Its nearly thornless canes and notably clean, vigorous foliage make it easier to handle and maintain than many English roses, and the bushy, upright shrub reblooms in generous flushes from late spring into early winter.

common_name: Oso Easy Double Pink Rose (Pure Pink Landscape Rose)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; Oso Easy Double Pink is part of the Proven Winners landscape rose series bred for disease resistance and low-maintenance repeat bloom.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun. Oso Easy Double Pink bears fully petaled, true pink blooms with soft yellow centers in dense, unstoppable flushes from late spring through frost on a compact, rounded shrub bred for strong resistance to powdery mildew and black spot. It needs no deadheading to keep blooming and no winter spray program to stay healthy, making it a practical choice for foundation plantings and mixed borders where low fuss matters. An annual light pruning in late winter keeps the plant tidy and floriferous.

common_name: Oso Easy Honey Bun Rose (Blush-to-Buttercream Landscape Rose)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; Oso Easy Honey Bun is part of the Proven Winners landscape rose series bred for disease resistance and low-maintenance repeat bloom.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun. Oso Easy Honey Bun produces semi-double blooms that shift through a soft mix of blush pink, buttery yellow, and creamy white as each flower ages, giving the compact, low-mounding shrub a pleasingly multicolored look through a single flush. It blooms continuously from late spring through frost without deadheading and holds clean, disease-resistant foliage through humid summers. A light shaping prune in late winter keeps the mounded habit dense and well-covered with flowers.

common_name: Oso Easy Urban Legend Rose (True Red Landscape Rose)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; Oso Easy Urban Legend is part of the Proven Winners landscape rose series bred for disease resistance and low-maintenance repeat bloom.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun. Oso Easy Urban Legend bears true red, semi-double blooms with prominent yellow stamens at the center, opening in long, continuous flushes from late spring through frost on an upright, well-branched shrub. Its vigorous, vertical habit makes it a useful thriller element in large containers as well as a strong color anchor in the border, and it holds disease-resistant foliage through the season with minimal spraying. Prune lightly in late winter to maintain shape and encourage fresh flowering growth.

common_name: Oso Easy Strawberry Crush Rose (Strawberry-Pink Landscape Rose)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; Oso Easy Strawberry Crush is part of the Proven Winners landscape rose series bred for disease resistance and low-maintenance repeat bloom.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun. Oso Easy Strawberry Crush opens large, double, self-cleaning blooms in a vivid strawberry pink that softens to a creamy pink as flowers age, giving the compact mounded shrub a two-toned effect across a single flush. It blooms repeatedly from late spring through frost without deadheading and resists the black spot and powdery mildew that plague older landscape roses. An annual light pruning in late winter keeps growth dense and covered in bloom.

common_name: Easy Elegance Kashmir Rose (Velvety Red Landscape Rose)

planting.note: Plant own-root or container roses in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Kashmir is part of the Easy Elegance landscape rose series bred for disease resistance and low maintenance, grown on its own roots.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun. Kashmir carries rich, velvety red blooms with the classic rounded, high-centered form reminiscent of hybrid tea roses, held above glossy green, disease-resistant foliage on an own-root shrub bred as part of the Easy Elegance series for garden performance without heavy spraying. It repeat-blooms through the season from late spring to frost, and because it grows on its own roots, any winter dieback simply regrows true to type. Deadhead spent blooms to encourage continued flushes and prune back by about a third in late winter.

common_name: Easy Elegance Sunrise Sunset Rose (Fuchsia-to-Apricot Spreading Landscape Rose)

planting.note: Plant own-root or container roses in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Sunrise Sunset is part of the Easy Elegance landscape rose series bred for disease resistance and low maintenance, with a dense, spreading habit suited to groundcover use.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun with room to spread. Sunrise Sunset bears bright fuchsia-pink petals that blend toward soft apricot near the center, giving each bloom a warm, sunset-like gradient, set against blue-green, disease-resistant foliage on a dense, spreading, own-root shrub. Its wide, mounding growth makes it one of the more vigorous Easy Elegance roses, useful as a flowering groundcover or bank cover rather than a small border shrub, and it blooms repeatedly from late spring through frost. Prune back hard in late winter to control size and renew flowering wood.

common_name: Easy Elegance My Girl Rose (Ruffled Deep Pink Landscape Rose)

planting.note: Plant own-root or container roses in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; My Girl is part of the Easy Elegance landscape rose series bred for disease resistance and low maintenance, grown on its own roots.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun. My Girl opens deep pink buds into ruffled, informal blossoms carried in generous clusters of five to thirty flowers per stem, held above medium green foliage noted for strong resistance to black spot. The compact, upright, own-root shrub repeat-blooms reliably from late spring through frost, and because it is grown on its own roots rather than grafted, winter dieback regrows true to type. Deadhead spent clusters to encourage continued flushes and prune back by about a third in late winter.

common_name: Easy Elegance Champagne Wishes Rose (Antique White Landscape Rose)

planting.note: Plant own-root or container roses in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Champagne Wishes is part of the Easy Elegance landscape rose series bred for disease resistance and low maintenance, grown on its own roots.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun. Champagne Wishes opens soft apricot buds into full, roughly three-inch blooms that fade to an antique white brushed with a hint of apricot, giving the own-root shrub a soft, old-fashioned look well suited to pairing with perennials in a mixed border. It repeat-blooms from late spring through frost on disease-resistant foliage bred to need little spraying, and because it is own-root, winter dieback regrows true to type. Deadhead spent blooms and prune back by about a third in late winter to maintain a full, well-flowered shape.
